construction.implementation_origin: New standalone implementation authored in the isolated build directory; no existing source read or copied.

input.fixture_label: Required nonblank string starting with synthetic, case-insensitive.

user.interests: Required object mapping at most 100 normalized tag names to integer weights 1..100; empty is allowed.

exclusions.item_ids: Required array of at most 1000 case-sensitive item IDs.
exclusions.categories: Required array of at most 100 normalized category names.
exclusions.tags: Required array of at most 100 normalized tags.

input.catalog: Required array of at most 1000 objects, each with exactly id, title, category, tags. IDs must be unique. Tags is an array of at most 100 strings.
input.limit: Required integer 0..100; booleans are not integers.

validation: validate_input is the shared validation and canonicalization entry point for both Python and CLI callers.
All object fields are required, with unknown fields rejected.
Strings must be nonblank and no longer than 200 characters before trimming.
All strings are trimmed; category and tag names are additionally casefolded. IDs remain case-sensitive.
Normalized duplicates in arrays, interests and catalog IDs are rejected.
CLI JSON parsing rejects duplicate keys, non-finite numeric constants, malformed JSON and invalid UTF-8.
Validation returns a fresh schema and never mutates the supplied input.

success_output.recommendations: Ordered array of rank (one-based), item_id, title, score, matched_interests and explanation.
success_output.matched_interests: Evidence entries containing tag, weight and source='catalog.tags', sorted by tag.
success_output.audit: catalog_count, eligible_match_count (before limit), unmatched_count (nonexcluded items without overlap), returned_count and excluded items with field/value reasons.

shared_schema.cli_contract: Exactly one JSON object on stdout. Success exit 0; validation, argument, encoding, parsing or file errors exit 2.

cross_stage_handoffs: Single functionality only; no external or cross-component handoff.
Within the functionality, validated canonical input passes through exclusion filtering, weighted preference ranking, evidence-based explanations and JSON output.
behavior: An ID exclusion, category exclusion or any tag exclusion vetoes an item regardless of preference score.
Only exact normalized tag intersections earn points; categories do not earn points.
Score is the sum of matched user weights. Nonmatching eligible items are not recommended.
Sort by descending score, then ascending case-sensitive item ID; apply limit only after filtering and ranking.
All exclusion reasons are retained. Excluded audit entries sort by ID.
Explanations state only matching catalog tags, supplied weights and the computed total; no generated product claims.
Empty catalogs, empty interests, zero limits and all-excluded catalogs return successful empty recommendations.
No fallback popularity ranking, randomness, implicit preferences or live LLM step.

included: Hard item, category and tag exclusions
Grounded structured evidence and human-readable explanations
Python API and UTF-8 JSON file CLI
excluded: Providers, network calls and LLM integration
Collaborative filtering and learned semantic similarity
Persistent profiles, inventory fetching and behavioral tracking
Authentication, serving infrastructure and concurrent processing

coverage: All three exclusion dimensions and veto precedence
Empty interests, empty catalog and zero limit
Invalid schema, types, bounds, duplicates and exclusions
Real subprocess CLI success, missing file and argument failures
Fixture-injected malformed JSON, duplicate keys, non-finite numbers and invalid UTF-8
